## Fresh Developments (Last 24–72h)

### Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Contract Pricing: HOT (bull)
TrendForce (June 1): Q1 2026 DRAM industry revenue **+81% QoQ**, reaching ~$97B. Conventional DRAM contract prices printed ~93–98% QoQ. Q2 2026 outlook: conventional DRAM **+58–63% QoQ** — still extreme but decelerating from the Q1 peak. HBM contract prices are tracking down YoY in 2026 under annual pricing mechanisms (pre-locked before memflation), but new 2027 HBM4 negotiations are actively underway with buyers.

### Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk: Nuanced (bull near-term; correction risk deferred)
TrendForce (June 2): Tight DRAM supply gives suppliers greater HBM pricing power — **HBM contract prices expected to "surge multiples higher in 2027."** This is a meaningful near-term upgrade vs. the baseline correction-risk signal, but the structural risk of over-supply post-late-2026 stands. SK Hynix pushed HBM4 capacity ramp from Q2 → Q3 2026 (HBM3E demand too sticky to convert). Samsung targeting ~250K HBM wafers/month by year-end (up ~47% from 170K current).

### Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex: Bull, no guide-downs
No first guide-down detected. **Meta raised 2026 capex to $125–145B** (from $115–135B), citing higher component pricing and added datacenter costs. Combined Google/Amazon/Microsoft/Meta 2026 capex now **$725B (+77% YoY)**, ~75% AI-directed (~$544B). Baseline range of $600–700B has been exceeded to the upside.

### Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASIC: Steady
No fresh MI400/Helios-specific news in last 72h. AMD on track for 2H-2026. **Marvell projects up to $11B in AI ASIC revenue for 2026**; Broadcom + Marvell control ~95% of custom AI ASIC co-design market — structural duopoly intact. AWS Trainium3 GA (3nm, 2.5 PFLOPS FP8, 144GB HBM3E). Google TPU v8 on schedule.

### Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics: Bull
**LITE CEO called 2026 "a breakout year for laser chip sales"** — sole volume supplier of 200G-per-lane EMLs for 1.6T transceivers. COHR showcased 1.6T transceivers at OFC 2026 across InP EML, silicon photonics, and GaAs VCSEL. InP supply gap remains ~70%. CPO mass deployment pushed to ~2028 (Broadcom's 10 pJ/bit energy target). Rothschild & Co. initiated ALAB + CIEN at Neutral ($153 PT for ALAB) — limited near-term upside signaled.

### Signal 6 — Solar/Power: Bull (FSLR-specific catalyst imminent)
**Section 232 polysilicon tariff ruling reportedly imminent (possibly June 2026).** Proposed: $10/kg on polysilicon, $0.07/W on ingots/wafers. Solar stocks +40% YTD ahead of the ruling. Roth Capital calls Section 232 a "positive catalyst" for **FSLR** — CdTe thin-film tech insulates it from polysilicon tariffs. US module pricing hit $0.28/W in Q1 2026; US-made cells command $0.46/W.

## Context vs. Baseline

- **DRAM memflation**: Q1 +81% QoQ industry revenue; conventional DRAM prices ~93–98% QoQ aligns with and meets the baseline +90–95% revision. Q2 deceleration to +58–63% is expected and healthy, not a signal of reversal.
- **HBM correction risk**: TrendForce's June 2 call for HBM to "surge multiples higher in 2027" is a constructive update — but capacity expansions completing late 2026 and HBM4 competition intensifying remain the baseline correction risk. Both signals are live simultaneously: 2026 tight, 2027 uncertain.
- **Hyperscaler capex**: $725B aggregate exceeds the $600–700B baseline range. Meta raise is an incremental positive.
- **Optical**: 70% InP supply gap and LITE's EML monopoly play out as expected. CPO 2028 timeline = no near-term disruption to pluggables.
- **Solar Section 232**: Not in the May 28 baseline but is the most actionable near-term binary for FSLR.

## Most Important Development

**TrendForce (June 2): HBM contract prices expected to "surge multiples higher in 2027"** — the single most significant update vs. the baseline correction-risk signal. Near-term this is a bull upgrade; the structural 2027 correction risk (capacity completing + HBM4 competition) is not eliminated but is deferred. Paired with MU +11% to a 52-week high and CRDO's Q4 blowout (+157% YoY), the AI memory and connectivity supercycle is printing above plan. Secondary watch: **Section 232 polysilicon tariff ruling (potentially June 2026)** — the single biggest near-term binary for FSLR and the broader solar complex.
